svg.aria-label: How to write ஞ: one unbroken stroke · 8 movements
svg.title: Writing ஞ
svg.desc: 8 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ஞ (tamil), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansTamil-Static.ttf. Stroke order after Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 8, ஞ (University of Texas at Austin), p. 194 <https://sites.la.utexas.edu/tamilscript/files/2009/08/hw_lettersinstructions.pdf>. Source note on variation: Appendix I Frame 8 numbers eight movements: 1–2 build the left inner loop, 3 draws the top bar, 4–5 form the shoulder and central descent, and 6–8 sweep around the broad outer bowl. Native writers draw them as one continuous stroke, and this ductus follows them in order without lifting: the pen starts inside the small loop and spirals out into the top bar, comes back along the bar to the central upright, and climbs back up that upright to where the outer bowl leaves it. In HP Labs India's online Tamil handwriting data (the LipiTk 4.0 Tamil isolated-character recognizer, trained on hpl-tamil-iso-char), 86% of the 140 stored prototypes of ஞ are a single pen-down stroke. Tamil handwriting varies by school; this is one attested order fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline.
svg.text: How it is written — one unbroken stroke · 8 movements
Stroke order after Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 8, ஞ (University of Texas at Austin), p. 194
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
